examples.code:
<Columns>
  {(['small', undefined, 'medium', 'large'] as const).map(size => (
    <Column key={size ?? 'normal'}>
      <Combobox label={size ?? 'normal'} size={size} inline>
        <Combobox.Input placeholder="Fruit" />
        <Combobox.Options>
          <Combobox.Option value="apple">Apple</Combobox.Option>
          <Combobox.Option value="banana" checked>
            Banana
          </Combobox.Option>
          <Combobox.Option value="cherry" disabled>
            Cherry
          </Combobox.Option>
        </Combobox.Options>
      </Combobox>
    </Column>
  ))}
</Columns>

accessibility:
- **The roles:** the field is `role="combobox"` with `aria-autocomplete="list"` and
  `aria-haspopup="listbox"`. The list is a `listbox` of `option`s, and a group is a `group` named by
  its heading. This is the ARIA 1.2 combobox the ARIA Authoring Practices describe.
- **Focus stays in the field:** the highlighted option is the field's `aria-activedescendant`.
  When a key or the list opening moves the highlight, the option is scrolled into view, since a
  browser only scrolls to what has focus. The pointer moves it without scrolling, since the pointer
  is already on that option. A click on an option keeps focus in the field too.
- **`aria-expanded`** is `true` while a list with an option in it is on screen, and
  `aria-controls` points at the list then. While the dropdown shows just `Combobox.Empty`, the
  field says it's collapsed, and so does the server markup for a list rendered with
  `appendToBody`, which shows only once the page has hydrated.
- **The list's name** comes from the label that names the field: the Combobox's `label`, or an
  outer `Field`'s. An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` you put on `Combobox.Options` wins, and
  with none of these the list is named "Suggestions".
- **`aria-selected`, with one value,** is on the highlighted option and nothing else, the way the
  Authoring Practices' combobox examples do it. The value shows as a check mark, which doesn't rely
  on color, and the list opens with the highlight on it. Several libraries put `aria-selected` on
  the chosen option instead.
- **With `multiple`,** the list is `aria-multiselectable`, and each option's `aria-selected` is its
  `checked`.
- **Disabled options** are `aria-disabled` and stay reachable with the arrows, the Authoring
  Practices' advice for listbox options, so a screen reader user finds them. They're never picked
  or `aria-selected`, and the opening highlight and `autoHighlight` pass over them.
- **The empty message** sits beside the list, not in it, so it isn't counted as an option. When
  your typing brings it on screen, its text is announced through a polite status region that's in
  the page from the start, once each time the matches run out. Opening the list with it already
  there, or emptying the field, announces nothing. While `isLoading` is on, or a loading `Control`
  is around the Combobox, the announcement waits and is made once loading ends. In a dropdown,
  keep it to text: Tab closes the list before a keyboard user can reach a link or a button in it.
  An `inline` list stays on screen, so a link or a button beside it is in the Tab order.
- **No counts are announced,** for the reasons in [A Result Count](https://bestax.io/docs/api/form/combobox#a-result-count).
- **Enter and Escape:** Enter submits the form when nothing is highlighted, and Escape only stops
  at the Combobox when it closed a panel that was on screen.
- **Forced colors:** in Windows high contrast mode the highlight is drawn as an outline in the
  system's highlight color, a disabled option takes the system's color for disabled text, and the
  check mark and the panel's edge stay visible.
- **No motion:** nothing animates.
summary: The `Combobox` component builds a text field with a list of options under it, for a searchable select, a server search, a multi-select or grouped options, with the keys and ARIA done and the data left to you. The app owns the data: what's in the list, how it's filtered, and the value. A pick calls `onOptionSubmit` with the option's `value`, and the Combobox keeps no value and never changes the text in the field, so the app sets both there. Nothing filters the options for you either, so a server's answer shows as it came. For a free-text field with suggestions, `Autocomplete` is the simpler choice. Focus stays in the field, and the highlighted option is its `aria-activedescendant`. With one value, the highlighted option is the `aria-selected` one, as the ARIA Authoring Practices' combobox does it, and a `checked` option shows a check mark and takes the highlight when the list opens. With `multiple`, `checked` is each option's `aria-selected`. Tab and focus leaving close a dropdown list without picking. When typing leaves `Combobox.Empty` on screen, its text is announced through a polite status region, once, after any loading ends. Result counts aren't announced: a screen reader reads the list's size from the markup, and a count on every keystroke talks over the typing. Show one in a `role="status"` line beside the field when it matters.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's label, which names `Combobox.Input` through `htmlFor`, and the list through `aria-labelledby`. Dropped inside an outer `Field`, whose label names both instead when it points at the field. When `Combobox.Input` has an `id` of its own, server markup names the field through `aria-labelledby` until the page hydrates and the label's `for` catches up.

props.name: labelProps
props.description: Props for the label element. An explicit `htmlFor` takes over the association: give `Combobox.Input` the same `id`, and the list is still named after the label.

props.name: children
props.description: The parts, in order: `Combobox.Input`, then `Combobox.Dropdown` with `Combobox.Options` and `Combobox.Empty` in it. With `inline`, the `Combobox.Options` and `Combobox.Empty` go straight in. Render `Combobox.Options` while there are options and `Combobox.Empty` while there aren't: the empty message sits beside the list, not in it.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. When set, opening and closing only report through `onOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the open state asked for: `true` from typing, a click in the field or Down Arrow, and `false` from Escape, Tab, a pick with one value, focus leaving or a press outside. Fires in controlled and uncontrolled use.

props.name: onOptionSubmit
props.description: Called with an option's `value` when it's picked with Enter or a click. A disabled option is never picked. The Combobox keeps no value and doesn't change the text in the field: update yours here.

props.name: autoHighlight
props.description: Highlights the first enabled option whenever the list opens or its options change, so Enter picks the top match. It only highlights: leaving the field still picks nothing, and so does Tab.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Several values can be picked. The list stays open after a pick, it's `aria-multiselectable`, and each option's `checked` is its `aria-selected`.

props.name: inline
props.description: The list is always on screen, in the flow under the field, as in a Popover or a page panel. There's no dropdown, so nothing closes it, and Escape goes to whatever is around it.

props.name: position
props.description: Where the dropdown opens against the field: below (`bottom-*`) or above (`top-*`), lined up with its left or right edge. `auto` picks the one that keeps the list in the viewport, preferring below. The same union Popover takes.

props.name: appendToBody
props.description: Renders the dropdown through `Portal`, into the `portalContainer` a `ConfigProvider` sets, `document.body` by default, fixed to the viewport at the field, so a container that clips its overflow can't cut it off. It then shows from the commit after hydration, never in server markup. Theming variables set on an ancestor reach it only when the portal's container is inside that ancestor, as with Popover. In a `Modal`, point `portalContainer` inside the modal, so the list stays in the dialog for assistive tech.

props.name: size
props.description: Sizes the field and the options together.

props.name: labelSize
props.description: Size for the label (used in horizontal layouts).

props.name: horizontal
props.description: Horizontal field layout.

props.name: message
props.description: Help/validation message below the input.

props.name: messageColor
props.description: Bulma color for the message.

props.name: fieldClassName
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the Field wrapper.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the `div.combobox` around the field and the list.

props.name: iconLeft
props.description: Icon props for left icon. Bulma gives control icons `pointer-events: none`, so a clickable node here never receives a click. Put a button beside the input in its own addon `Control` instead.

props.name: iconRight
props.description: Icon props for right icon. Bulma gives control icons `pointer-events: none`, so a clickable node here never receives a click. Put a button beside the input in its own addon `Control` instead.

props.name: iconLeftName
props.description: Shortcut for left icon name.

props.name: iconRightName
props.description: Shortcut for right icon name.

props.name: iconLeftSize
props.description: Shortcut for left icon size.

props.name: iconRightSize
props.description: Shortcut for right icon size.

props.name: hasIconsLeft
props.description: Force left icon container.

props.name: hasIconsRight
props.description: Force right icon container.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows a loading spinner on the `Control` it renders. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the spinner stops and stays drawn (with bestax's CSS loaded). The spinner sits at the right edge, where `iconRight` also sits, and the two overlap; leave the right icon out while loading.

props.name: isExpanded
props.description: Expand the control.

props.name: controlSize
props.description: Control size.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the Control.

props.name: color
props.description: Bulma color modifier for the input.

props.name: isRounded
props.description: Rounded input corners.

props.name: isStatic
props.description: Styles the input as static text. It stays editable; add `readOnly` to stop edits.

props.name: isHovered
props.description: Applies hovered state.

props.name: isFocused
props.description: Applies focused state.

parts.summary: The floating panel under the field, on screen while the list is open and its children aren't all empty.

props.name: children
props.description: What the panel shows: `Combobox.Options` while there are options, and `Combobox.Empty` while there aren't. Children that are all `null`, `false` or `''`, or empty Fragments, keep the panel shut, so write the conditional here. A component that renders nothing, or a `Combobox.Options` with no options in it, still counts, and shows an empty panel.

props.description: Additional CSS classes.

parts.summary: One choice in the list, with a check mark while it's `checked`.

props.name: value
props.description: What `onOptionSubmit` hands back. Unique within the Combobox.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Can't be picked. The arrows still reach it, so a screen reader user finds it, and it's never `aria-selected`.

props.name: checked
props.description: It's the value, or one of them. It shows a check mark, the list opens with the highlight on it, and with `multiple` it's the `aria-selected`.

props.name: children
props.description: What the option shows: text, or text with an avatar, a tag or a hint.

props.description: Additional CSS classes.
